newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin net debt rose in H1 on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Michelin net debt rose in H1 on stocks.

text.p: Tyremaker Michelin said its net debt rose to 23.2 billion francs in the first half of 1996 from 21.6 billion francs at the end of June 1995, reflecting a buildup in tyre inventories.
It said its stocks-to-turnover ratio rose to 90.8 at the end of the first half of 1996 from 80.4 a year earlier, prompting the company to slow down production to reduce its stocks.

Finance Director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere told a news conference that the company's net debt at the end of August was below August 1995 levels, "so we're moving in the right direction." He did not give a debt figure for August.
He said the inventory buildup was due to the fact that Michelin "overestimated the demand in Europe, particularly in trucks."

If subordinated debt is included in overall debt, the debt to equity ratio was 1.97, compared with 2.61 in the first half of 1995. If the subordinated debt is grouped with equity, the ratio went to 1.21 in the first half of 1996 from 1.4, he said.
The company earlier reported its financial expense declined in the first half of 1996 to 737 million francs from 804 million due to lower interest rates.

Bourdais de Charbonniere said the share of fixed costs as a percentage of turnover had declined in the first half of 1996 to 39 percent from 43.5 percent in the first half of 1993 as a result of the group's cost-cutting strategy.
He said staff levels were around 2,000 below the year-earlier total of 114,700 and said he expected little change in the figure between now and the end of the year.
